title.narrative: Anticipatory integrated health, nutrition, and WASH action in response to projected poor rains in Raso woreda, Somali region, Ethiopia

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtThe objective of the project is to implement an anticipatory integrated health, nutrition, and WASH response in Raso woreda of the Somali region to mitigate the impacts of projected poor rains during the October – December 2024 season. It seeks to address acute malnutrition, improve water access, and prevent WASH-related diseases such as cholera while strengthening local health and water management systems to build resilience among vulnerable populations.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtConcern Worldwide requests a total budget of $520,000 to implement the project for the duration of six months (November 2024 to April 2025). Through this support, an estimated total of 66,081 vulnerable people (20,072 girls, 19,253 boys, 12,421 women, and 11,935 men), of whom an estimated total of 63 people are people with disabilities, will directly benefit from WASH, health, and nutrition activities.ltbrgtThe project is implementing WASH interventions to improve access to safe water and promote hygiene among vulnerable communities.ltbrgtHealth activities will increase measles immunization coverage for children aged 9 to 59 months, particularly as communities in crisis face heightened risks of infectious disease outbreaks due to weakened health systems, malnutrition, and limited access to clean water and sanitation. By focusing on vaccinating zero-dose children—those who have not received any prior doses—the intervention addresses these vulnerabilities, reducing the risk of measles outbreaks and protecting public health. The campaign also supports broader public health goals, including achieving herd immunity, which protects those unable to be vaccinated, such as infants under nine months or immunocompromised individuals. By raising overall community immunity, the intervention mitigates disease transmission and outbreak risks, especially in densely populated areas. The measles immunization efforts complement initiatives to address malnutrition and improve water access. The WASH intervention, combined with support for Public Health Emergency Management through the health program, will be instrumental in managing and preventing outbreaks, particularly cholera.ltbrgtThe nutrition component focuses on reducing malnutrition-related morbidity and mortality particularly among U5 children. By strengthening community awareness of malnutrition screening and improving early detection through mass screenings, the project ensures acute malnutrition cases are promptly identified and treated. Capacity-building efforts will enhance the local health systems' ability to manage Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) cases at stabilization centres and through outpatient therapeutic programs.ltbrgtThe project will mainstream protection, PSEA, prevention of GBV, and gender equality to contribute to the social and psychological well-being of women and girls. It will prioritize protection against gender-based violence (GBV) through prevention, mitigation, and response. Concern has strict policies on protection, including a code of conduct, a protection mainstreaming policy, and a PSEA policy. All field staff receive training on these policies to ensure full compliance and are equipped with the skills to appropriately capture and refer protection issues. Concern will employ female staff in field teams and implement activities in a culturally and gender-appropriate manner to prevent GBV. The project will also ensure that persons with disabilities are carefully identified and included in health and nutrition activities, CRM processes, and project review sessions.ltbrgtThis project complements CERF-funded initiatives in the woreda. We will engage with CERF partners to ensure coordinated action and that lessons are continually shared on the complementary approach between EHF and CERF. Concern will implement the project through coordination and collaboration with local stakeholders, authorities and coordination structures.lt/pgt
